summary: A sculpted human heart (checked by a University of Dundee anatomist) showing the external features of the heart with both coronary circulations painted on: coronary arteries in red and cardiac veins in blue. The great cardiac vein climbs beside the anterior interventricular artery, the middle cardiac vein accompanies the posterior interventricular artery, and both drain into the coronary sinus in the posterior coronary sulcus. The great vessels are colour-coded by oxygen content: red = oxygenated (aorta, pulmonary veins), blue = deoxygenated (venae cavae, pulmonary arteries).
clinical: The coronary sinus opens into the right atrium between the inferior vena cava opening and the tricuspid valve. Cardiologists cannulate it to place the left-ventricular lead of a biventricular (resynchronisation) pacemaker in a lateral cardiac vein, and surgeons use it to give retrograde cardioplegia.

The anterior interventricular artery supplies the anterior left ventricle, the apex and the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum, so a proximal LAD occlusion causes a large anterior infarct.

SubTool-0.name: Heart
SubTool-0.description: The whole heart is a single sculpted mesh with the vessels painted on: coronary arteries red, cardiac veins blue, on a pale myocardium. On the back the coronary sinus runs in the coronary sulcus to the right atrium beside the inferior vena cava, receiving the great, middle and small cardiac veins and the posterior (inferior) vein of the left ventricle; small anterior cardiac veins cross the right coronary artery to drain straight into the right atrium. Arterially the pattern is right-dominant: the right coronary artery gives the posterior interventricular artery.

notes: Single ZBrush mesh with the anatomy painted in vertex colour, so it cannot be split into parts; all structures are listed on the one part. Although titled an external view, the painting shows the cardiac veins as well as the coronary arteries (Sketchfab thumbnail agrees). Right dominance judged from the posterior-inferior view (the RCA reaches the crux and gives the posterior interventricular branch). The blue veins on the anterior right ventricle crossing the right coronary artery were read as anterior cardiac veins. Colours: the painted vertex colours render paler (myocardium near-white, blue vessels lavender) than on Sketchfab, where the myocardium is pink-red; this looks like a vertex-colour colour-space difference in the importer, and a curation colour override would wipe out the painting, so it was left alone.
